predecessors.name: Mongol Khanate
predecessors.text: the Right Wing pastures that Altan, 'the de facto leader of the whole of the Right Wing' since 1542, held when he forced the Great Khan's successor to flee eastward in 1547

successors.name: Later Jin dynasty
successors.text: the Tumed plain at Hohhot, which 'submitted to the Qing dynasty' (Tumed page) in the early 17th century; the Manchus gained control of the Inner Mongolian tribes in 1635 (Inner Mongolia page)

ledger.x: 1547: Altan takes the Right Wing and drives the Great Khan east.

1552: the rest of Cliopatria's enlargement: Inner Mongolia outside the Hohhot plain (the Ordos and the plains west and east of it) and the south Gobi, 2,403 cells less the Hohhot disc already added in 1547, taken from the Khalkha shape.
1582: Altan dies and the Tumed realm shrinks.
1582: the rest of Altan's realm, outside Hohhot, returns to no state.
1635: the Manchus take control of the Tumed lands.
1635: the Tumed state ends and becomes the Guihua Tümed banner.

wars.name: Altan Khan's wars with the Ming
wars.outcome: Altan besieged Beijing in 1550 ('crossed gaps in the Great Wall and besieged Beijing, setting its suburbs on fire') and in 1571 'made peace with the Ming China to open large markets'; the Hohhot page has the blockade ended in 1570 'by establishing a…

wars.name: Tumed recapture of Karakorum from the Oirats
wars.outcome: Altan Khan gained control of the remains of Karakorum in 1552.

wars.name: Ligdan Khan's campaigns against the Tumed and the Later Jin
wars.outcome: Ligdan razed Guihua in 1631 and 'successfully attacked the Khorchin and the Tümed'; in 1632 Hong Taiji and his Mongol allies marched against him; Ligdan died in 1634 and his son surrendered in 1635.

certainty.note: The steppe frontiers are approximate; the Tümed plain at Hohhot is the one fixed point (town, temples of 1557 and 1579).
